packages/observe/src/guard.ts's evaluateGuard() DOES return a structured, typed result (`GuardResult = { decision: GuardDecisionKind, reason: string }`, where `GuardDecisionKind = z.enum(["allow", "block", "review"])`, defined in packages/core/src/schema.ts). This is a real, stable, documented decision-kind enum — a materially better answer than 'throws an opaque error or returns empty', which is what API-008 is written to catch. However, the `reason` field is a free-text `string`, not an enumerated, stable reason CODE (e.g. "tool \"x\" is on the blocked-tools list" is human-readable prose, not a code like `BLOCKED_TOOL_NAME` a caller could safely switch on across versions without string-matching). API-008's Pass criterion explicitly asks for 'Enumerated reason codes, stable, documented' — the decision kind meets that; the reason does not. Recommend: add a stable `reasonCode` field (enum) alongside the existing free-text `reason`, so callers get both machine-actionable and human-readable information. This is a Medium finding per the doc's own fixed severity, not newly invented — it should be added to the findings list, not left in skipped_unverified, since real evidence (the actual type definitions) was found.

new_findings_not_in_first_pass.finding: Traced the one live pre-execution control this codebase actually has — evaluateGuard(), called from ObservingTransport.send() in packages/observe/src/mcp.ts:151-159 — for fail-closed behavior on an internal throw. There is no try/catch around the `evaluateGuard()` call or around `this.blockOutbound()`. If evaluateGuard were to throw (e.g. a pathological regex in `blockedArgumentPatterns` throwing, or `safeStringify` throwing on a cyclic args object), the exception propagates out of `send()` before `this.inner.send(message, options)` is ever reached on the next line — meaning a throw in the guard control structurally CANNOT result in the call reaching the real transport. This is genuine fail-closed behavior, verified by code reading (a throw aborts the function before the forwarding call, there is nothing that could catch-and-continue). BUT: no test in packages/observe/src/mcp.test.ts actually forces evaluateGuard/safeStringify to throw and asserts the call was not forwarded — I grepped mcp.test.ts for throw/toThrow/rejects and found no fault-injection case. Per §3.6 this is legitimate Code evidence (I named the specific control-flow reason a catch→proceed can't happen), but it falls short of the Verify method the doc itself specifies ("Fault-injection tests... assert the call is denied"). Recommend the software-engineer or qa-engineer add exactly that test before this is closed with Test evidence rather than Code evidence alone.

new_findings_not_in_first_pass.check_id: GOV-001 / spec-scope (informational, not a numbered checklist item)
new_findings_not_in_first_pass.finding: docs/security-check.md §1.1 and §2.1 describe the system as a live, synchronous interceptor sitting between model output and tool execution ('Intercepts model-emitted tool calls before execution... Executes or forwards the call'), and its ten attack scenarios (A1-A10) are largely framed around that live-interception model. Reading the actual package boundaries (packages/core = schema/policy/evidence/store, packages/decision = LLM-backed decision/escalation/fix-proposer, packages/assertions = post-hoc transcript assertions, packages/observe = the one place with live interception — proxy.ts, guard.ts, mcp.ts) shows the codebase is predominantly a POST-HOC auditor of already-captured agent transcripts (assertions, evidence packs, calibration, reporters), with exactly one live pre-execution control (`evaluateGuard` in packages/observe) rather than the fully live validate-then-autofix-then-execute pipeline the spec's system description assumes throughout. This does not invalidate any individual finding above, but it explains why several checks (API-006, API-008, API-004) map awkwardly onto the actual code — they were written for a system with a live autofixer 'rewriting calls' (§1.2's central risk framing, A2), and there is currently no autofixer in the live tool-call path at all (AFX-* checks are in the undefined-section gap the first pass already flagged, which may not be a coincidence). Recommend the Human Gatekeeper decide whether docs/security-check.md's system description needs a §11 amendment to match what's actually built, or whether the live-interception surface (packages/observe) is intended to grow to match the spec over time — either is a legitimate answer, but leaving it unstated makes several checks unfalsifiable in either direction.
